points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 勒内·笛卡尔1596年3月31日出生于法国图赖讷地区的拉哈耶（现更名为笛卡尔市）。他的父亲是布列塔尼议会的议员，母亲在他出生后不久去世。笛卡尔由外祖母抚养长大，接受了良好的早期教育。这段时期，他展现出对知识的强烈好奇心，尤其是对数学和科学的兴趣。虽然身体虚弱，但他的智力发展迅速，为后来的哲学思想奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: René Descartes was born on March 31, 1596, in La Haye en Touraine (now Descartes), France. His father was a member of the Brittany Parliament, and his mother died shortly after his birth. Descartes was raised by his maternal grandmother and received an excellent early education. During this period, he demonstrated a strong curiosity for knowledge, particularly in mathematics and science. Despite being physically frail, his intellectual development progressed rapidly, laying the foundation for his later philosophical ideas.

points.place: 法国拉弗莱什耶稣会学校
points.title: 教育启蒙
points.description: 笛卡尔进入著名的拉弗莱什耶稣会学校接受教育，这是当时欧洲最好的学校之一。在这里，他学习了古典文学、哲学、数学、物理学和天文学等学科。虽然他接受了传统的亚里士多德哲学教育，但逐渐对其中的一些教条产生了怀疑。这段教育经历使他认识到知识的确定性问题，并开始思考如何建立一种可靠的认识论基础。他后来回忆说，这是他思想形成的关键时期。
points.descriptionEn: Descartes entered the prestigious La Flèche Jesuit School, one of the best educational institutions in Europe at the time. There, he studied classical literature, philosophy, mathematics, physics, and astronomy. Although he received traditional Aristotelian philosophical education, he gradually became skeptical of some of its dogmas. This educational experience made him aware of the problem of certainty in knowledge and began to ponder how to establish a reliable epistemological foundation. He later recalled that this was a crucial period in the formation of his thoughts.

points.title: 游学探索
points.description: 1618年，笛卡尔离开法国开始游历欧洲，先后在荷兰、德国、丹麦和波兰等地生活。在荷兰，他遇到了数学家贝克曼，两人建立了深厚的友谊，并在数学和物理学方面进行了合作。笛卡尔在这一时期发展了他的解析几何思想，这是数学史上的重大突破。他还参与了军队服役，在荷兰与法国的战争中担任军事工程师。这段经历使他接触到不同文化和思想，拓宽了他的视野，同时也促使他思考如何将数学方法应用于哲学问题。
points.descriptionEn: In 1618, Descartes left France to travel across Europe, living in the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, and Poland. In the Netherlands, he met mathematician Beeckman, with whom he developed a deep friendship and collaborated in mathematics and physics. During this period, Descartes developed his ideas on analytic geometry, a major breakthrough in the history of mathematics. He also served in the military as an engineer during the Dutch-French war. This experience exposed him to different cultures and ideas, broadening his horizons and prompting him to think about how to apply mathematical methods to philosophical problems.

points.title: 思想成熟
points.description: 1628年，笛卡尔移居荷兰，并在那里度过了20年，这是他思想最活跃、成果最丰硕的时期。他先后在海牙、代尔夫特、恩德霍芬和莱顿等地居住。在荷兰，笛卡尔可以自由地思考和写作，不受宗教和政治迫害。他完成了《方法论》、《形而上学的沉思》和《哲学原理》等重要著作，系统阐述了他的理性主义哲学体系。他还与当时欧洲许多重要学者保持通信交流，包括惠更斯、霍布斯和伽利略等人。荷兰时期是笛卡尔学术生涯的黄金时期，他的哲学思想在这里得到了充分发展和完善。
points.descriptionEn: In 1628, Descartes moved to the Netherlands, where he spent 20 years, the most active and fruitful period of his thought. He lived successively in The Hague, Delft, Eindhoven, and Leiden. In the Netherlands, Descartes could think and write freely without fear of religious and political persecution. He completed important works such as 'Discourse on Method,' 'Meditations on First Philosophy,' and 'Principles of Philosophy,' systematically expounding his philosophical system of rationalism. He also maintained correspondence with many important European scholars of the time, including Huygens, Hobbes, and Galileo. The Dutch period was the golden age of Descartes' academic career, where his philosophical ideas were fully developed and perfected.

points.title: 方法论革命
points.description: 1637年，笛卡尔在荷兰莱顿出版了他的重要著作《方法论》（全名为《关于正确引导理性在科学中探索真理的方法论》）。这本书包括三个附录：《几何学》、《折光学》和《气象学》，其中《几何学》部分首次系统阐述了解析几何的思想。笛卡尔在《方法论》中提出了著名的四条方法论原则：1) 只接受清楚明白地呈现到心灵中的事物；2) 将复杂问题分解为简单部分；3) 从简单到复杂进行推理；4) 全面检查推理过程，确保没有遗漏。这些方法不仅影响了哲学，也深刻改变了科学研究的范式，被视为科学革命的重要推动力。
points.descriptionEn: In 1637, Descartes published his important work 'Discourse on Method' (full title 'Discourse on the Method of Rightly Conducting One's Reason and of Seeking Truth in the Sciences') in Leiden, Netherlands. The book included three appendices: 'Geometry,' 'Dioptrics,' and 'Meteorology,' with the 'Geometry' section systematically expounding the ideas of analytic geometry for the first time. In the 'Discourse on Method,' Descartes proposed his famous four methodological principles: 1) Only accept what is clearly and distinctly presented to the mind; 2) Divide complex problems into simple parts; 3) Reason from simple to complex; 4) Examine the reasoning process thoroughly to ensure nothing is omitted. These methods not only influenced philosophy but also profoundly changed the paradigm of scientific research, seen as an important driving force of the Scientific Revolution.

points.title: 晚年岁月
points.description: 1649年，笛卡尔应瑞典女王克里斯蒂娜的邀请前往斯德哥尔摩，担任她的哲学导师。然而，北欧严寒的气候和女王要求每天清晨五点在寒冷的城堡里授课，严重损害了笛卡尔本已虚弱的健康。1650年2月，笛卡尔因肺炎去世，享年53岁。尽管在瑞典的时间短暂，但笛卡尔仍然完成了《论灵魂的激情》等著作。他的去世被视为哲学界的重大损失，他的思想却继续影响着后世哲学和科学的发展。
points.descriptionEn: In 1649, Descartes was invited to Stockholm by Queen Christina of Sweden to serve as her philosophy tutor. However, the harsh Nordic climate and the queen's requirement of teaching at 5 AM in the cold castle seriously damaged Descartes' already fragile health. On February 1650, Descartes died of pneumonia at the age of 53. Despite the short time in Sweden, Descartes still completed works such as 'The Passions of the Soul.' His death was seen as a great loss to the philosophical community, but his ideas continued to influence the development of later philosophy and science.

appraisal.zh: 笛卡尔被尊为近代哲学之父，其理性主义体系为西方哲学奠定新基础，「我思故我在」确立了主体性在认识论中的核心地位，方法论原则为科学研究提供系统框架，解析几何则推动了数学发展。不过也有研究者指出，其二元论难以解释心物如何相互作用，方法论偏重理性演绎而轻视经验观察，机械论宇宙观后来被牛顿力学与量子力学超越；亦有看法认为其思想并非全然原创，而是融合经院哲学、古代怀疑论与新兴科学方法而成。
appraisal.en: Descartes is honored as the father of modern philosophy: his rationalist system laid a new foundation for Western thought, 'I think, therefore I am' established subjectivity at the center of epistemology, his methodological principles gave scientific inquiry a systematic framework, and analytic geometry advanced mathematics. Yet researchers also point out that his dualism struggles to explain mind-body interaction, that his method favors rational deduction over empirical observation, and that his mechanistic cosmos was later surpassed by Newtonian and quantum mechanics; another view holds that his thought was not wholly original but fused scholastic philosophy, ancient skepticism and the new science.

supporter.zh: 笛卡尔被誉为'近代哲学之父'，他的理性主义哲学体系为西方哲学奠定了新基础。他提出的'我思故我在'确立了主体性在认识论中的核心地位，开创了以理性为基础的哲学传统。笛卡尔的方法论原则为科学研究提供了系统框架，他的解析几何将代数与几何结合，推动了数学的发展。他的二元论思想虽然受到批评，但启发了后世对心物关系问题的深入探讨。笛卡尔的思想遗产不仅限于哲学领域，还深刻影响了科学、数学和现代认知科学的发展。
supporter.en: Descartes is hailed as the 'father of modern philosophy,' and his rationalist philosophical system laid a new foundation for Western philosophy. His proposition 'I think, therefore I am' established the central position of subjectivity in epistemology,开创ing a philosophical tradition based on reason. Descartes' methodological principles provided a systematic framework for scientific research, and his analytic geometry combined algebra and geometry, advancing mathematical development. Although his dualism has been criticized, it inspired later in-depth explorations of the mind-body problem. Descartes' intellectual legacy extends beyond philosophy, profoundly influencing the development of science, mathematics, and modern cognitive science.

critic.zh: 笛卡尔的哲学体系受到多方面批评。他的二元论被指责无法解释心物如何相互作用，导致后世哲学家如斯宾诺莎、莱布尼茨等人试图修正这一理论。他的方法论过于强调理性演绎，忽视了经验观察的重要性，受到经验主义者的批评。笛卡尔对数学确定性的过度推崇也受到质疑，因为数学公理本身也需要经验验证。此外，他的'清楚明白'标准被认为过于主观，难以作为可靠的认识论基础。在科学史上，笛卡尔的机械论宇宙观后来被牛顿力学和量子力学所超越，显示出其历史局限性。
critic.en: Descartes' philosophical system has been criticized from multiple perspectives. His dualism is accused of failing to explain how mind and body interact, leading later philosophers like Spinoza and Leibniz to attempt to revise this theory. His methodology overemphasizes rational deduction while neglecting the importance of empirical observation, drawing criticism from empiricists. Descartes' excessive emphasis on mathematical certainty has also been questioned because mathematical axioms themselves require empirical verification. Furthermore, his standard of 'clear and distinct perception' is considered too subjective to serve as a reliable epistemological foundation. In the history of science, Descartes' mechanistic worldview was later surpassed by Newtonian mechanics and quantum mechanics, revealing its historical limitations.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，笛卡尔常被符号化为理性主义和科学精神的象征。他的名言'我思故我在'已成为西方文化中最著名的哲学命题之一，代表着人类对自我意识的觉醒。笛卡尔的形象在流行文化中常与理性、怀疑精神和科学探索联系在一起，成为启蒙运动的先驱代表。然而，历史学家也指出，笛卡尔的思想并非完全原创，而是融合了中世纪经院哲学、古代怀疑主义和新兴科学方法的结果。他的哲学体系虽然具有开创性，但也反映了17世纪欧洲特定的历史背景和知识传统，需要在历史语境中理解其意义。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Descartes is often symbolized as an embodiment of rationalism and scientific spirit. His famous quote 'I think, therefore I am' has become one of the most well-known philosophical propositions in Western culture, representing humanity's awakening to self-consciousness. Descartes' image in popular culture is frequently associated with reason, skepticism, and scientific exploration, representing a pioneer of the Enlightenment. However, historians also note that Descartes' thoughts were not entirely original but rather a fusion of medieval scholastic philosophy, ancient skepticism, and emerging scientific methods. Although his philosophical system was groundbreaking, it also reflected the specific historical context and intellectual traditions of 17th-century Europe and needs to be understood within that historical context.
